title: Ca(OH)₂ vs bacteria: who survives the tubules?
topic: Ca(OH)₂ is pH 12.5 at the canal, but dentine buffers OH⁻, so E. faecalis deeper in the tubules can survive (in vitro).

claims.source: Mohammadi Z, Dummer PMH, Int Endod J 2011;44:697–730 (PMID 21535021)

claims.claim: Ca(OH)₂ ⇌ Ca²⁺ + 2OH⁻: the solid slowly releases ions (lattice drawing is schematic)
claims.source: Mohammadi Z, Dummer PMH, Int Endod J 2011;44:697–730 (PMID 21535021)

claims.claim: pH 11.5 line: kills E. faecalis (in vitro)
claims.source: Evans M et al., Int Endod J 2002;35:221–8 (PMID 11985673); McHugh CP et al., J Endod 2004;30:218–9 (PMID 15085049)

claims.claim: OH⁻ diffuses into the tubules; some nearby cells turn red (PI uptake = membrane breached)
claims.source: Nerwich A et al., J Endod 1993;19:302–6 (PMID 8228751); Parmar D et al., Int Endod J 2011;44:644–51 (PMID 21352240)

claims.claim: High pH likely damages membranes, proteins and DNA (proposed mechanisms)
claims.source: Siqueira JF Jr, Lopes HP, Int Endod J 1999;32:361–9 (PMID 10551109); Mohammadi Z, Dummer PMH, Int Endod J 2011;44:697–730 (PMID 21535021)

claims.claim: Dentine buffers OH⁻: the pH front stalls
claims.source: Haapasalo HK et al., Int Endod J 2000;33:126–31 (PMID 11307453); Nerwich A et al., J Endod 1993;19:302–6 (PMID 8228751)

claims.claim: pH model: ≥ 11.5 only at the canal wall, inner dentine about 10.8, outer dentine slow to rise (7.2 → 8.1 by day 7)
claims.source: Toy model / schematic: anchored to Nerwich A et al., J Endod 1993;19:302–6 (PMID 8228751); clock and depth compressed

claims.claim: E. faecalis survives pH 11.1; proton pumping (H⁺ in) appears critical
claims.source: Evans M et al., Int Endod J 2002;35:221–8 (PMID 11985673)

claims.claim: Killing near the canal is partial; E. faecalis survives below the 11.5 line
claims.source: Haapasalo M, Ørstavik D, J Dent Res 1987;66:1375–9 (PMID 3114347); kill pattern hand-placed (schematic)

claims.claim: Takeaway: pH is the weapon, dentine is the shield; past the canal wall, E. faecalis can survive (in vitro)
claims.source: Nerwich A et al., J Endod 1993;19:302–6 (PMID 8228751); Evans M et al., Int Endod J 2002;35:221–8 (PMID 11985673); Haapasalo M, Ørstavik D, J Dent Res 1987;66:1375–9 (PMID 3114347)

caption:
Who survives a Ca(OH)₂ dressing?
The paste sits near pH 12.5, but dentine buffers the OH⁻ that diffuses in: inner root dentine peaked at only pH 9.7–10.8.
In vitro, E. faecalis survives pH 11.1 but not 11.5; its proton pump seems key.
So killing near the canal wall is partial, and cells deeper in the tubules can persist (in vitro data). The clinical benefit of the dressing is still debated.
Refs: Mohammadi & Dummer 2011, Int Endod J · Nerwich 1993, J Endod · Haapasalo et al. 2000, Int Endod J · Evans 2002, Int Endod J · Haapasalo & Ørstavik 1987, J Dent Res · Sathorn 2007, Int Endod J
